free_tier.stated: Free API with no key: 600 calls a minute, 5,000 an hour, 10,000 a day and 300,000 a month, covering the forecast, air quality, elevation, flood, geocoding and marine APIs and the historical weather (ERA5 from 1940), historical forecast, climate, ensemble, seasonal and satellite radiation APIs.
free_tier.notes: A request over 10 weather variables or over 2 weeks of data for one location counts as more than one call, in fractions (15 variables over 2 weeks count as 1.5 calls). Bulk path: the AWS open-data bucket s3://openmeteo in us-west-2 holds the model archives as .om files and listed with no credentials.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: the unit is a request

retention.stated: not applicable: the unit is a request

egress.terms: not applicable: JSON answers counted as calls; the s3://openmeteo bucket listed with no credentials, and its transfer price was not read

interface_detail: REST over HTTPS GET with query parameters, JSON answers and no key; the archive at archive-api.open-meteo.com; the bulk archive in the public AWS bucket s3://openmeteo (us-west-2) as .om files
tooling: any HTTP client; any S3 client reads the bucket anonymously, and .om files are read with the Open-Meteo OM-file readers for Python, Rust, Swift and TypeScript. Last resort: the user installs and runs the open-source AGPLv3 server on a rented or free machine.
chaining: A keyless point-weather and reanalysis source: forecasts and ERA5 history per coordinate under a 10,000-call daily cap, with the full model archive in a public S3 bucket for bulk pulls.

limits.value: limits counted per IP address and application; callers on a shared egress can be limited earlier

binding_note: 10,000 calls a day binds a steady poller: 600 a minute reaches the 5,000 hourly cap in under 9 minutes, 5,000 an hour reaches 10,000 in 2 hours, and 10,000 a day over 30 days equals the 300,000 monthly cap.

identity_cost.detail: No API key, no sign-up and no credit card. GET requests with no credentials answered HTTP 200 from the forecast and archive endpoints, and the s3://openmeteo bucket listed with no credentials.

reliability_note: Applications and IP addresses can be blocked without prior notice; the free API carries no uptime target.
confidence_note: Limits and licence are read from first-party pages; the forecast and archive endpoints answered HTTP 200 with JSON to calls with no key, and an anonymous ListObjectsV2 on s3://openmeteo answered HTTP 200. The 10,000-a-day ceiling was not driven to its limit.
